description: The Auroral Rampart is a standing wall of green-violet fire nearly a light-hour across, curtaining a dead magnetar's wound in the firmament. Curtains of plasma roll along its face in braids bright enough to cast measurable light across the whole system, and hulls in the outer orbits glow faintly at night. No photograph has ever captured the same pattern twice.

The tempest convulses on a rough fifty-three-hour rhythm, but the volatility lives in the detail: filaments lash out without warning and discharge fronts outrun every forecast. Ships touching the curtain suffer instant avionics death and hull charging that ends in arcing discharges between masts. Crews caught in prolonged exposure tell of power cells singing in resonance until they burst.

The Rampart was born nine million years ago when the magnetar's field snapped through its own crust, and the storm has simply never stopped. The mining cluster Halde Nord was erased in 2226 when a discharge front arrived ahead of all warnings, an event that rewrote sector storm-handling law. Storm-chaser crews now work its fringes for exotic ion states that sell for fortunes.

Magnetar monitoring stations ring the system at twenty-six million kilometers, an amount of caution most pilots consider minimal. The Rampart shows no sign of aging; its ninth million year differs from its first only in the constellations reflected along it. Sailors give the wall its due distance and read its beauty through filters, from very far away.
